newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise on debt buyback hopes.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise on debt buyback hopes.

text.p: Argentine bonds were well bid in early trading Monday driven by talk of a debt buyback scheme, dealers said.

"After Reuters quoted (Economy Minister Roque) Fernandez talking of a possible debt buyback, the market perked up and it will continue to stay firm as long as that rumor exists," a trader at a leading local bank said.

In an interview released Monday Fernandez said "conditions are right" for Argentina to buy back foreign debt for the first time, following in the footsteps of Brazil which launched a buyback earlier this year. But he gave no more details.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/2 to 95, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was firm at 121.60.

Traders said sharp gains on the New York markets after Friday's U.S. Independence Day holiday also boosted sentiment, with long bond yields falling to 6.57 percent from 6.62 percent Thursday and the Dow jumping 0.6 percent.
"It looks like a good day with a lot of demand from investors abroad, so we should see decent trading volumes," another dealer said.
